title: Progressive output-shape synthesis and Zod/JSON Schema interop for TypeScript client
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Our TypeScript client currently leaves structured output validation to downstream apps (ad-hoc zod schemas or manual checks). This causes field-level regressions, subtle contract mismatches, and poor streaming ergonomics for discriminated unions. The goal of this ticket is to provide a pragmatic path that combines compile-time type generation with small, well-tested runtime artifacts (Zod + JSON Schema) to enable safe progressive parsing of streaming responses and robust runtime validation for non-streaming flows.

Problem statement:
- Generated types can diverge from runtime shapes (especially for polymorphic unions, optional discriminator placement, and streaming delta chunks).
- Developers struggle to use discriminated unions over streaming outputs: runtime guards are either heavyweight or brittle.
- Existing codegen outputs are large and hard to maintain across model updates.
- We lack a migration story for existing customers relying on untyped responses.

Goals:
1) Generate TypeScript types + companion Zod schemas and compact JSON Schema artifacts from model output contracts.
2) Provide streaming-friendly runtime validators that can progressively validate partial chunks using discriminator hints.
3) Ensure backcompat: opt-in migration with feature flags, clear deprecation path for older helpers.
4) Keep runtime overhead low (~<200B gzipped per schema bundle) and provide lazy-loading hooks for server/client bundlers.

Out of scope: full AJV integration for arbitrary JSON Schema features (we only support the subset needed for outputs: type, required, enum, properties, discriminator, oneOf/anyOf limited to small unions).
proposal:
High-level approach:
1) Contract-first shape spec: accept a lightweight, developer-authored 'output shape' DSL (YAML/JSON) or infer shapes from prompt examples during onboarding.
2) Codegen will produce: (a) TypeScript types, (b) Zod validators (z.object/z.union with discriminators), (c) a minimized JSON Schema that mirrors the Zod shape for external tooling.
3) Streaming runtime: build a small 'progressive guard' runtime that accepts discriminator hints and validates partial fragments. The runtime exposes two APIs: validateFull(output) -> {ok|error} and validatePartial(fragment, hint) -> {ok|needMore|error}.
4) Union strategy: require an explicit discriminator key by default (configurable). When missing, we emit a generated 'tag' extractor that looks for shape markers (presence of specific properties) with an ordered fallback list.
5) Bundling/size control: emit schemas as separate artifacts and expose lazy imports (e.g. import('./schemas/my-thing-schema')). Then TS client will expose a small 'useSchema' helper to load validators on demand.
6) Migration: default to no-op. New flag `enableOutputValidation: \"opt-in\" | \"warn\" | \"enforce\"` controls behavior. When warn/enforce, we log runtime mismatches (with sampling) and optionally throw for enforce.

Implementation notes: codegen will live under packages/ts-client/codegen. Zod version locked to 4.x. JSON Schema output targets draft-07 subset. The progressive runtime will be implemented in packages/ts-client/runtime and instrumented into streaming helpers (packages/ts-client/streaming).
acceptance_criteria: Codegen emits TypeScript types + Zod validators + JSON Schema for a sample 'MyThing' contract.
A streaming progressive guard API exists and demonstrates partial/complete validation on a sample discriminated union with >95% accuracy on synthetic test corpus.
Runtime bundle size for a representative schema bundle is < 2KB gzipped when lazy-loaded; non-lazy baseline < 15KB gzipped.
Backwards-compat migration flag implemented: opt-in | warn | enforce with telemetry for mismatches.
Integration tests covering: union discriminator present, discriminator absent with fallback rules, malformed streaming chunks, and graceful degradation when validators are missing.
Documentation and a short migration guide published in docs/redwood/ts-client/output-validation.md and example PR linking it.
notes: We should measure common consumer patterns (embeddings -> rerank -> structured) to decide which shapes to eagerly bundle.
Consider a small runtime written in plain JS (no external deps) with TypeScript declarations to minimize locking to zod at runtime; zod schemas still generated for convenience.
Edge case: streaming arrays of union items require per-item discriminator hints; we will implement an indexed hint API to avoid revalidating full items repeatedly.
We will add a sampling pipeline to forward failure telemetry (anonymized tokens + schema id) to the console for improving shape contracts over time.
